THE BUG (analyze.py, introduced 2026-08-17, live for one day): _excursion_stats() normalised MFE/MAE/realised by t['sl'] -- the stop AFTER the ratchet rewrites it -- while _r_of() correctly used sl_orig. The ratchet only rewrites the stop on trades that armed it, i.e. only on winners, so this was not noise but a one-sided bias that flattens the fat tail. SOL (closed 2026-08-17 +2.476R) printed MFE +0.98R and realised +0.99R against a true +2.46R / +2.48R. Every loser read correctly, which is why it was invisible in aggregate. Corrected: >=1.0R now 3/11 (was 2/10), >=2.0R now 2/11, and the trail armed in 2/11 overall -- but 2 of 6 (33%) under the CURRENT exit regime, which is the only rate that describes the deployed system. The trail is engaging roughly a third of the time, not a tenth. The entry-is-the-problem thesis is weakened, not confirmed.
INVARIANT ADDED: MAE <= realised <= MFE is true by construction (a trade cannot exit above its own peak) and was violated by SOL for a full day. Now asserted every night with a 0.10R tolerance for poll sampling; the bug it would have caught put SOL 1.50R over. A derived metric that never checks its own arithmetic is how a measurement bug survives a review that is looking straight at it.
